rule: GOAL: Align colored plus shapes so their arms cover matching dots. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the active shape; space switches to the next shape. RULE: A plus is solved only when every dot of its color lies on one of its arms. TRAP: Assuming the plus center must land exactly on an intersection; arms can cover dots without the center touching them.

GOAL: Navigate the grid from start to finish using limited moves. CONTROLS: Arrow keys slide you two cells in the chosen direction. RULE: You only move if both the immediate and destination cells are open. TRAP: Believing you slide until blocked wastes time; movement is strictly two cells.

GOAL: Align the gray shape so its yellow section fits perfectly into the wall's yellow gap, connecting the upper and lower gray areas. CONTROLS: Click the bottom blue button to shift the gray shape left; click the top button to shift it right. RULE: The yellow blocks must match in width and position to bridge the gap and complete the circuit. TRAP: Trying to move the shape vertically or horizontally far enough to cover the entire board wastes time; only specific alignment works.

GOAL: Fill both cups by pouring fluid into their notches. CONTROLS: Arrows slide the bar; space pours the fluid. RULE: Fluid flows off the bar's ends, so align the bar ends directly above the cup gaps. TRAP: Believing the fluid falls from the bar's center or sides rather than dripping off the tips.

GOAL: Guide two plugs to align their dots with specific cross targets simultaneously. CONTROLS: Click to extend or retract a plug’s length by fixed increments. RULE: Both dots must occupy their designated cross centers at the same time to win. TRAP: Assuming a single dot landing on a cross clears the level; both must be positioned together.

GOAL: Align three scattered shapes to specific target coordinates on the grid. CONTROLS: Arrow keys shift the highlighted shape three spaces; Spacebar cycles the active shape. RULE: The white dot always marks the current center, providing immediate feedback on position. TRAP: Assuming shapes block each other; they overlap freely, so ignore collisions when planning moves.

GOAL: Move the purple bead along the dotted rail to the target hole. CONTROLS: Clicking a dot on the rail within range moves the bead there. RULE: Clicks only work if the dot is close enough to the bead’s current position. TRAP: Clicking distant dots wastes turns; the bead does not jump far or ignore distance limits.

GOAL: Move three shapes to cover specific dots. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the active shape; space cycled to the next shape. RULE: Each shape only covered dots on its own geometric path, not filled areas. TRAP: Assuming shapes covered all dots inside their bounds wasted time on impossible placements.

GOAL: Stack two boxes to complete the frame. CONTROLS: Arrows move the character; Space grabs or releases a box. RULE: Grabbing flips the cap to the top, letting you lift boxes over walls. TRAP: Moving with a box attached shifts the whole stack, not just the box.

GOAL: Match five pink glyphs to their blue counterparts by cycling through options. CONTROLS: Left and right arrows move the selection cursor between columns; the up arrow cycles the current glyph’s shape. RULE: Each column requires a specific shape class, identified by comparing the pink and blue glyph patterns. TRAP: Assuming the cursor position is static or that shape options cycle independently per column without checking the current state first.

GOAL: Clear the level by moving the player up, left, and up again to bypass the trap. CONTROLS: Arrows move the player one tile in the chosen direction. RULE: The trap lunges exactly two tiles left when triggered by proximity in its row. TRAP: Assuming the trap chases the player; it actually moves left regardless, so do not expect it to follow you vertically.

GOAL: Route fluid streams into three cups by swapping bar positions and sizes. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected bar; Space pours fluid; Mouse clicks swap two bars. RULE: Streams flow straight up; bars must align with cup notches and avoid blocking other paths. TRAP: Assuming bars stay in place; forgetting to move the upper bar clears the path for the middle stream.

ESTABLISHED: The head moves up in six-row increments, stopping at row 12. The rail sits at row 14. FAILED: Extending the arm from below pushes blocks sideways instead of carrying them. GOAL IS NOT: Simply aligning the arm's height with the rail without lateral clearance. CONTROLS: Up moves the head; Left retracts the arm; Right extends it, pushing blocks if they collide.

ESTABLISHED: The tray holds five nails. The board is a nine-column checkerboard. The initial tray pattern is black, white, black, white, white. FAILED: Mapping tray colors to the bottom row, top row, or middle columns of the board failed. Using "all black" or "any black" logic for nail groups failed. GOAL IS NOT: Matching the vertical column pattern. Matching the simple alternating sequence. Matching the bottom row directly. CONTROLS: Clicking nails toggles their color between black and white. The timer bar depletes with each move.

GOAL: Move the X-shape to touch the green zone, then return it home. CONTROLS: Arrow keys slide the shape across the grid. RULE: Only the shape's tips matter; the center can float freely. TRAP: I assumed the whole shape must stay clear, but only the tips trigger color changes.

GOAL: Navigate a grid to destroy three directional traps and reach the exit without triggering their attacks. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved the player one step in the cardinal direction to position for destruction or evasion. RULE: Traps lunged along their eye direction only if the player stood within two squares of that ray. TRAP: Assuming eyes tracked the player; they were static, meaning fixed rays defined safe zones, not relative positions.

GOAL: Clear the level by managing the shrinking pink bar while navigating around fixed walls. CONTROLS: Clicking blue blocks moved them; other clicks were ineffective. RULE: The pink bar decreased by one unit per action, enforcing a strict step limit. TRAP: Assuming clicking doors, plugs, or walls would trigger mechanics wasted precious steps.

GOAL: Match each colored button to its corresponding empty dot to complete the pattern. CONTROLS: Press SPACE to select a color from the bottom row, then press SPACE again to place it on a target dot. RULE: The game ends automatically once all four dots hold the correct matching colors. TRAP: Believing you must manually press a final submit button; placement is immediate, and extra actions waste time.

GOAL: Rotate the yellow block to the fixed bracket position. CONTROLS: Red arrow rotates the ring counter-clockwise; green arrow rotates it clockwise. RULE: Each click moves the ring one step; aligning the block with the bracket completes the level. TRAP: Wasting moves by rotating back and forth instead of calculating the shortest path first.

GOAL: Clear the board by jumping pegs over adjacent neighbors into empty spaces, removing the jumped pegs until only one remains. CONTROLS: Click a peg to select it and reveal valid landing spots, then click a landing spot to execute the jump. RULE: A jump is valid only if an adjacent peg sits between the current peg and an empty space two steps away. TRAP: Assuming clicking empty spaces moves the peg; you must click the landing marker, not the destination cell directly.

GOAL: Fill seven color slots in a specific order. CONTROLS: Click items to swap positions; press space to submit the arrangement. RULE: The path flows through the red box, down the stem, and across the green box before the final slot. TRAP: Assuming the green box fills right-to-left wastes time guessing the wrong item order.

GOAL: Drop the purple blob into the circular ring. CONTROLS: Click a target to move the white cursor there; clicking the green orb swaps the two positions. RULE: The purple piece always moves halfway between the white and green markers, so align them to guide it. TRAP: Thinking the purple piece follows the cursor directly, when it actually mirrors the cursor across the green orb.

GOAL: Place seven colored tiles to match a hidden sequence by following path redirects through linked boxes. CONTROLS: Click buttons to pick up colors, click slots to place them, and press space to submit. RULE: When a slot is blocked, the sequence jumps to the linked box, fills it entirely, then returns. TRAP: Assuming strict left-to-right reading order ignores the gap redirects, causing mismatches in the final positions.

ESTABLISHED: Filling the plus shape triggers success when the green set matches it exactly; success clears the grid to gray. FAILED: Clicking the reference box when the grid contains green cells does nothing; clicking the center when surrounded by green does nothing. GOAL IS NOT: Simply clicking the reference box or filling arbitrary patterns; the specific plus shape must be the sole active pattern. CONTROLS: Clicking a cell toggles its color; clicking the reference box loads a pattern only when the grid is entirely gray.

GOAL: Place the plug and fill remaining slots so the pre-filled green block aligns with item three in the sequence. CONTROLS: Click tray items to select them, click empty slots to place them, and press space to validate the solution. RULE: The pre-filled block dictates the sequence order, forcing the plug into the third red slot to maintain continuity. TRAP: Assuming the plug fits any red slot; placing it elsewhere breaks the sequence alignment and requires restarting the level.
GOAL: Match panel D to its mini pattern. CONTROLS: Click cells to toggle red or blue. RULE: White means blue, green means red. TRAP: Assuming clicking the mini hint changes the board.

GOAL: Align the rotating legend to match the target before reaching the box. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the block; covering the plus symbol rotated the legend. RULE: You must repeatedly cover the plus to cycle the legend into the correct orientation. TRAP: Assuming movement alone solves the puzzle; ignoring the legend alignment wastes turns and fails the level.

GOAL: Match the main grid to the hidden pattern encoded by two mini-grids. CONTROLS: Click cells to cycle their color between red and blue. RULE: The top mini maps to the top three rows; the bottom mini maps to the bottom two rows. TRAP: Assuming the orange center of the mini is a playable color; it is just a marker.

ESTABLISHED: Two black squares exist. Merging them creates a solid 10x5 block. The maze has specific black paths and a central gap. FAILED: Moving the merged block without rotation. Trying to fit the horizontal block into the central gap. GOAL IS NOT: Placing the merged block directly into the central bottom gap as-is. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move blocks. Spacebar rotates the merged block 90 degrees, changing its shape to vertical.

GOAL: Move yellow tokens to bottom row. CONTROLS: Red arrows shift rows; green arrows reverse shifts. RULE: Clicks apply fixed permutations to grid cells. TRAP: Green arrows are not manual undo buttons; they trigger specific inverse permutations.

GOAL: Fill the grid with Red or Orange to match hidden color codes. CONTROLS: Click cells to toggle colors; inspect mini-panels for clues. RULE: A mini’s center color applies to its White cells; the other color applies to its Gray cells. TRAP: Assuming Gray always means background; here, Gray takes the opposite color of the mini’s center.

ESTABLISHED: The door is solid for the player everywhere. The right-room box is permanently stuck. FAILED: Moving the player into the left frame interior did not clear the level. GOAL IS NOT: Simply placing the player on the left frame interior. CONTROLS: UP is a no-op that consumes steps; LEFT and DOWN move the player.

ESTABLISHED: A red snake occupies the right side, leaving the left column open. A blue ring sits at the bottom right. FAILED: Moving down the left column is blocked by a gray barrier at the second row down. GOAL IS NOT: Reaching the gray block or interacting with the snake directly. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the blue square one grid step. Spacebar rewinds to the last checkpoint.

GOAL: Place yellow and orange blocks into their matching colored brackets. CONTROLS: Left and right red buttons spin rings counterclockwise; green buttons spin them clockwise. RULE: Shift a ring so a block enters the shared center, then shift the other ring to pull it across. TRAP: Assuming blocks stay on one ring; they only transfer when passing through the central connection point.

GOAL: Route two separate chains so their midpoints land on specific colored rings. CONTROLS: Clicking an empty spot moves the active node; clicking another chain’s node swaps positions between chains. RULE: Swapping nodes between chains changes no chain’s midpoint, allowing repositioning without breaking existing alignments. TRAP: Moving a node away from its chain’s center disrupts the midpoint; use swaps to shift active nodes while keeping chain geometry intact.

GOAL: Move both blocks to the top bar. CONTROLS: Arrows push both blocks simultaneously. RULE: Blocks slide until hitting walls or each other. TRAP: Assuming independent movement; they are locked together.

GOAL: Align the plug’s tips precisely onto the socket terminals to complete the circuit. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the entire plug assembly across the grid. RULE: The plug must fit exactly to the left of the green zone without overlapping it. TRAP: Assuming prongs could cross into the green area; they must stop just short at the boundary.

GOAL: Move the mirrored piece to align perfectly with the yellow target zone. CONTROLS: Arrow keys shift both pieces simultaneously; the second piece moves in the opposite horizontal direction. RULE: One press moves pieces three cells; left-right inputs mirror across the central divider. TRAP: Assuming pieces move independently; they are linked, so you must calculate combined trajectories.

GOAL: Match the big grid to the hidden pattern using the three-color rule. CONTROLS: Click cells to cycle colors; click mini-grids to reveal their specific mapping. RULE: White in a mini means paint with that mini's center color; green means paint with the opposite. TRAP: Assuming the color cycle order is fixed; each mini defines its own unique color translation.

GOAL: Guide two separate squares to occupy adjacent positions on the board. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move both squares simultaneously in the chosen direction. RULE: Vertical moves shift both squares in the same direction, not mirrored. TRAP: Assuming vertical moves mirror the second square causes invalid paths and wasted time.

ESTABLISHED: The token starts at the bottom. Red and blue blocks rotate when buttons are pressed. The blue block currently blocks the exit hatch. FAILED: Moving the token directly toward the top yellow token fails because the path is blocked by background gaps. GOAL IS NOT: Simply walking the token to the yellow item on the current floor layout. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the token. Clicking buttons rotates the corresponding colored block, changing walkable paths and carrying the token if it stands on the block.

GOAL: Move the charcoal block to the target zone by reflecting the black block across a movable mirror. CONTROLS: Arrows move the mirror when locked, or the black block when unlocked; Space toggles the lock state. RULE: Position the mirror so the reflection aligns with the target before unlocking and moving the block. TRAP: Assuming arrows always move the block wastes time; you must first set the mirror position while locked.

GOAL: Reach the yellow target by crossing shifting colored zones. CONTROLS: Arrows move the token; clicks rotate red or slide blue blocks. RULE: Rotate the red arm before walking on it to create a vertical bridge. TRAP: Assuming the red arm sweeps safely; it crushes the token if rotated while you are on it.

GOAL: Reach the pink cross in the upper room. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player; clicking breaks obstacles. RULE: Touching the cross triggers a win. TRAP: Assuming the cross blocks movement; it is a goal, not a wall.

ESTABLISHED: Canvas holds purple top and white V. Block is purple. FAILED: Upright placement paints rows 32-38 only; depth did not adapt to canvas content. GOAL IS NOT: Matching the card image directly or sinking deeper when painted. CONTROLS: Arrows rotate block. Space places it. Clicking card did nothing.

GOAL: Arrange four nodes into two separate chains using twelve clicks. CONTROLS: Click a node to swap it with yours; click empty space to move your node there. RULE: Swapping preserves geometry while exchanging positions, allowing you to rearrange without moving nodes physically. TRAP: Assuming you must move every node individually wastes actions; use swaps to instantly reposition nodes into place.

GOAL: Slide two L-shaped pieces so their holes reveal matching yellow targets on the other side of the mirror. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the active piece; Space cycles selection between the two shapes. RULE: Only the selected piece moves; unselected pieces stay fixed until you switch to them. TRAP: Assuming holes stay white when placed. They turn yellow when aligned, making it hard to see if the piece is still active.

GOAL: Route three shapes—Plus, X, and Diamond—to match their target colors. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active shape; Space cycles to the next one in order. RULE: Shapes change color only when their path touches a matching color swatch. TRAP: Assuming Space cycles randomly; it strictly follows a fixed sequence, so plan your switch order carefully.

GOAL: Arrange four horizontal bars to form a continuous path for liquid to fill three cups. CONTROLS: Click a bar to select it, then use arrow keys to slide it horizontally. RULE: Bars must not overlap or block flow; they must align precisely to channel the liquid without gaps. TRAP: Assuming bars could pass through each other or that vertical alignment mattered more than horizontal connectivity.

GOAL: Align two bead-bearing pieces and a mirror so reflections land on yellow targets. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active piece; Space cycles active pieces. RULE: Reflections only appear below the mirror; move the mirror down first to reveal the reflection zone. TRAP: Assuming pieces block each other; they pass through mirrors and targets, so order matters more than collision.

GOAL: Align three separate white regions with their respective blue markers. CONTROLS: Click blue blocks to shift height between adjacent white regions. RULE: Each click transfers two units of height from the left region to the right one. TRAP: Assuming you must fill every white space; actually, only specific alignment matters, so empty regions are fine.

GOAL: Turn the entire grid purple by matching a hidden target pattern. CONTROLS: Click cells to flip them and their neighbors; click special cells to flip only themselves. RULE: Special cells must remain purple, forcing their click state, which then dictates the rest. TRAP: Assuming all cells follow standard neighbor-flipping rules ignores the special cells' isolated behavior.

GOAL: Move the white diamond into the blue chain's empty slot. CONTROLS: Click a node to select it, then click a target slot to swap or move. RULE: Swaps exchange positions between any two chains, not just within one. TRAP: Assuming white nodes retain their color when moved; they adopt the target chain's hue.

GOAL: Fill the yellow area using the piece and its reflections. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active object; Space cycles between the piece and mirrors. RULE: The piece must align perfectly with the yellow target for reflections to complete the shape. TRAP: Believing reflections could cover yellow while the piece itself remained outside the target zone.

GOAL: Align two mirrored pieces to perfectly fill the yellow target shape. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active object; Space switches between the piece and the mirror. RULE: The mirror reflects the piece across its axis; position the mirror so reflections complete the pattern exactly. TRAP: Assuming the mirror position is fixed; you must move the mirror itself to align the reflection axes correctly.

GOAL: Transform a row of glyphs to match a hidden pink word by cycling each position through the alphabet. CONTROLS: Left and Right arrows move the cursor between glyph slots; the Up arrow advances the current glyph to the next letter in the sequence. RULE: Each glyph cycles independently through the alphabet, so you must align each slot’s letter count to match the target word’s structure exactly. TRAP: Assuming the cursor stays put after moving; failing to reposition before cycling wastes actions and misaligns the final word.

GOAL: Decipher the hidden message by rotating blue glyph rows to match the target sequence derived from the yellow legend. CONTROLS: Arrow keys rotate the selected glyph row; confirm to lock the row in place. RULE: Yellow words dictate the blue target order, where word length equals the number of blue positions to fill. TRAP: Assuming legend values were simple identifiers; they were actually complex rotation dictionaries, causing failed matches until properly decoded.

GOAL: Transform the seven glyphs to match the target sequence. CONTROLS: Arrows move the cursor; pressing UP cycles the current glyph’s shape. RULE: Each glyph cycles through a fixed sequence of seven shapes, so you count the steps needed to reach the target. TRAP: Assuming the cycle order is identical for every position wastes time; always verify the current shape before pressing.

GOAL: Guide the key to the socket while keeping the energy bar alive. CONTROLS: Arrows move the key one step at a time. RULE: Energy drains constantly; you must revisit the refill ring to restore power before visiting the final target. TRAP: Visiting the ring too early or too often wastes moves, risking death before reaching the socket.

GOAL: Arrange symbols into their target rows using only vertical shifts. CONTROLS: Clicking a column moves the top symbol to the bottom of that same column. RULE: Each column operates as an independent circular loop, ignoring horizontal neighbors. TRAP: Assuming rows connect horizontally or wrap around to adjacent columns causes infinite loops.

GOAL: Fit two shapes onto yellow blocks using mirror symmetry. CONTROLS: Arrows move pieces, Space toggles mirrors. RULE: Mirror axis is fixed; pieces must align perfectly with the reflection line. TRAP: Calculating moves from normalized shape coordinates instead of absolute grid positions wastes actions.

GOAL: Move two yellow blocks into the top corner brackets. CONTROLS: Top arrows rotate the small top row; bottom arrows shift the entire outer ring. RULE: The board wraps around edges, allowing blocks to travel across boundaries along the cycle. TRAP: Assuming green arrows reset the board; they actually reverse the specific shift direction.

GOAL: Guide the lamp to the bottom board and use its internal peg to jump into the target cell, leaving exactly one peg on the board. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the lamp along the wire; clicking selects or confirms the final jump action. RULE: The lamp acts as an extra board cell when docked, allowing a jump that removes the obstacle peg. TRAP: Believing the lamp must enter the board grid; it stays docked outside, enabling the jump from the edge.

ESTABLISHED: The plug area matches the yellow object's internal void exactly. The plug fits perfectly inside the yellow shape's bounding box, completing the rectangle. FAILED: Standard socket insertion at symmetric points yields no win. Covering red contacts or simple overlap logic fails. GOAL IS NOT: Inserting the plug into a visible socket or matching external shapes. CONTROLS: Dragging the plug aligns it with the yellow object. Snapping occurs when the plug fills the yellow shape's empty space completely.

ESTABLISHED: Grabbing and releasing the orange costs two actions each time. Boxes move in parallel with you, potentially blocking your path or parking permanently if obstructed. FAILED: A rigid pre-planned route for all five boxes and the orange failed due to unexpected path collisions and timing issues. GOAL IS NOT: Simply activating all boxes; the last slot must remain empty for the manually carried orange. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player. Space releases the held object. Re-grabbing requires positioning and pressing Space again.

GOAL: Arrange colored items and plugs to match the tray exactly. CONTROLS: Click slots to swap items; press space to validate. RULE: Plugs redirect flow, consuming items not placed in the tray. TRAP: Assuming every tray item must be placed visibly ignores hidden consumption.

ESTABLISHED: The action bar shows used steps against a limit. Purple and yellow-white-yellow cells kill on contact. A crate blocks the shaft. FAILED: Rising in the left room or shaft hits the ceiling traps. The horizontal chain route is too long for the budget. GOAL IS NOT: Surviving the ceiling traps by timing rises. CONTROLS: Move moves the player. Break destroys the crate. Actions consume the bar.

ESTABLISHED: Movement is rigid. If either square hits a wall or the other, the pair stays put. FAILED: Assuming independent movement or partial slides. Trying to force a move when one path is blocked wastes time. GOAL IS NOT: A simple single-square puzzle. You cannot separate the squares permanently; they act as one connected unit. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move both squares simultaneously in the same direction until a blockage stops the entire pair.

GOAL: Route colored plugs to matching boxes while filling empty slots with correct items. CONTROLS: Click tray items to select, then click grid slots to place. Press space to submit. RULE: Plugs in the main box must match the color of the target box they feed. TRAP: Assuming tray position dictates order; instead, plug color determines which box receives the flow.

GOAL: Rotate the long bar to reach the yellow box. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the token; clicking podiums rotated bars. RULE: Standing on a pivot allows rotation; stepping on a mini podium activates it. TRAP: Believing the mini podium was an exit. It was just a switch to rotate the next bar.

GOAL: Route a seven-item flow through red, green, and blue boxes to fill all slots correctly. CONTROLS: Click tray items to place them in box slots or install color-diverting plugs. RULE: Plugs redirect the flow to their matching color box; empty target boxes absorb items, full ones discard them. TRAP: Believing flow continues naturally; ignoring plug placement causes the sequence to break or items to vanish prematurely.

ESTROLISHED: The orange moves two cells per action. Its path follows a strict parity rule that creates an impassable barrier under standard movement rules. FAILED: Assuming the orange pauses at boundaries. Assuming the orange only moves when the player is in the same column. Assuming the orange sweeps through intermediate cells. GOAL IS NOT: Simply stepping into a cell the orange will occupy in the next step, unless the death was caused by running out of time. CONTROLS: Player movement consumes one action. The orange moves two cells per action. Step budget depletes with each player move.

ESTABLISHED: The green plug's dot sits at row 31, columns 51-53, requiring the dot at row 31. FAILED: Layered searches fail due to variable resets; manual macro moves and simple greedy paths hit dead ends. GOAL IS NOT: Simply reaching the right edge or aligning colors, as the specific dot coordinate is strict. CONTROLS: Buttons extend or retract plugs, moving the attached dot; blocked actions consume turns without effect.

GOAL: Match the pink word by finding its two identical glyphs. CONTROLS: Arrows rotated the tiles to reveal different letters. RULE: The two-letter word required two adjacent tiles to be rotations of the same letter. TRAP: I assumed the visible shapes were different letters, missing that they were just rotated versions of the same glyph.

GOAL: Paint the lower canvas band purple while keeping the top section white. CONTROLS: Arrow keys rotate the block's orientation; mouse clicks select colors; spacebar stamps the current color. RULE: Rotating the block changes which side of the bracket it occupies, determining the stamp location. TRAP: Assuming the block returns to upright after a single rotation; it requires two specific turns to reset.

GOAL: Guide the player to the exit while avoiding a moving orange obstacle. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved the player one step per turn; the orange moved simultaneously. RULE: You cannot occupy a cell at the same time the orange moves into it, forcing timed detours. TRAP: Assuming you could pass through the orange's current location, which caused collisions and wasted moves.

GOAL: Align the colored markers to their matching target slots by navigating the rotating ring and radial arms. CONTROLS: Clicking the ring rotates all markers one step clockwise; clicking an arm moves markers between inner and outer tracks. RULE: Rotating the ring shifts every marker simultaneously, so you must group markers by track before rotating to the final position. TRAP: Assuming arm clicks only affect the specific marker clicked, when they actually shift the entire radial line, potentially displacing aligned markers.

GOAL: Slide the blue block into the matching socket. CONTROLS: Arrows move the block; covers shift when pushed. RULE: Passing over the color pad permanently dyes the block to match the socket. TRAP: Believing the pad consumes the block or changes shape; it only recolors it.

GOAL: Align the claw to the exact limit and fill the grid pattern to trigger the win. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the claw; clicks toggle grid cells. RULE: The win requires the claw to be clamped at the boundary while the correct pattern is formed. TRAP: Assuming the plus pattern is the goal; it was a trap that cleared progress without winning.

ESTABLISHED: Growth to 4x4 fails when the 3x3 is adjacent to the circle. Growth succeeded previously at distance 3. FAILED: Placing the 3x3 directly next to the circle with one donor inside. GOAL IS NOT: Simply having a donor inside the circle regardless of the 3x3's position. CONTROLS: Clicking near a piece moves it. Clicking near the donor restores it.

GOAL: Fill a grid with three colors matching specific diagonal patterns. CONTROLS: Arrows rotated the view; mouse selected paint; space applied it. RULE: Colors filled cells where row plus column met a specific sum threshold. TRAP: Applying colors in the wrong order erased earlier work; lower thresholds must be painted first.

GOAL: Clear the level in two moves by pushing the block upward. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the block; left and right rotate it. RULE: Rotating the block into a vertical stack aligns it with the narrow passage above. TRAP: Believing you must fill a pattern or click cells; the block simply needs to be rotated and pushed.

GOAL: Solve the puzzle by aligning specific colored tiles into their target positions. CONTROLS: Clicking the top button cycles column tiles forward; clicking the bottom button cycles them backward. RULE: The top and bottom buttons perform inverse three-way rotations on the same set of tiles. TRAP: Mistaking these rotations for simple two-tile swaps due to duplicate colors hiding the actual movement pattern.

GOAL: Move the peg through the winding track to reach the final dock. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the peg along the connected path; clicks execute jumps. RULE: The peg only travels along the continuous line; walls block direct paths. TRAP: Assuming you can move freely across the grid ignores the track’s specific turns and connections.

GOAL: Combine two separated purple blocks into one solid yellow square. CONTROLS: Click empty space to move a block toward that spot. RULE: A moving block absorbs any stationary block it touches or comes very close to. TRAP: Thinking distance checks are exact; ensure the moving block is clearly closer to the click point than the target block to avoid the target moving instead.

GOAL: Paint the canvas using specific colors and shapes. CONTROLS: Arrows rotate the stamp; Space presses it; Click selects colors or triggers small blocks. RULE: Rotate to align the stamp’s shape with the target region before pressing. TRAP: Assuming small blocks stamp automatically on every press; they only stamp when clicked directly, not via Space.

GOAL: Reach the purple podium to unlock the final button. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the token; clicks activated unlocked buttons. RULE: Stepping on a colored podium reveals that color’s button. TRAP: The magenta button teleports you across portals instead of moving objects.

GOAL: Guide the blocky claw into the handle’s inner slot. CONTROLS: Arrows move the claw; moves rotate it automatically. RULE: The 4x4 claw fits only when aligned with the grayed-out connector path. TRAP: Ignoring rotation makes diagonal paths fail; stick to straight lines through cleared zones.

GOAL: Paint the canvas with four colors to match the target pattern. CONTROLS: Arrow keys rotate the stamp, Space applies it, number keys pick colors. RULE: Each press fills a specific geometric region based on the stamp’s rotation. TRAP: Thinking the small block stamp is fixed; it actually moves with rotation, requiring precise positioning.

GOAL: Move the crate into the frame's interior. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active crate; clicks switch control. RULE: The active crate passes through frame walls; inactive ones do not. TRAP: Assuming all crates move simultaneously or that inactive crates can cross barriers.

GOAL: Paint the board with four colors using geometric regions. CONTROLS: Click swatches to pick colors, Space to paint, Arrows to tilt the board. RULE: Tilting changes which cells are visible, letting you paint specific diagonal zones. TRAP: Assuming the board is static; ignoring the tilt mechanic prevents isolating the required regions.

GOAL: Move the Y and p tiles into their matching target circles without colliding. CONTROLS: Click near a tile to move it a short distance toward the click. RULE: Deliver one tile completely before moving the other to avoid accidental merging. TRAP: Assuming you can route both simultaneously; close proximity causes reverts and wasted clicks.

GOAL: Guide the ink to the cap by aligning the claw. CONTROLS: Arrows move the claw; clicks rotate its pointing direction. RULE: Passing over a green cell absorbs its ink, enabling the final release. TRAP: Assuming the claw must stay adjacent to the rod; it must move to the cap after absorbing.

GOAL: Move the dot to the exit by shifting plugs to clear the path. CONTROLS: Click a plug to extend it; click again to retract it. RULE: Extending pushes overlapping plugs; retracting pulls adjacent plugs in the opposite direction. TRAP: Believing retracting leaves neighbors untouched; it actually drags them, requiring careful order to avoid blocking the path.

GOAL: Arrange three colored blocks into a single line on the arm. CONTROLS: Arrows move blocks; extend or retract the arm to shift grouped blocks. RULE: Blocks caught inside the arm move together with the tip, keeping their spacing. TRAP: Thinking you must push blocks individually; once grouped, they shift as a unit.

GOAL: Move the claw to the target socket and draw lines to complete the circuit. CONTROLS: Arrows move the claw; clicks finalize drawn segments to burst old pipes. RULE: The green bar on the right depletes with every action; you must finish before it empties. TRAP: Assuming movement is cheap; each arrow press costs budget, so plan paths before moving.
